title: Compile base-function guards as assumptions
motivation: GNU-R's `BASEGUARD` checks that a call like `sum(...)` still calls the base function. bc2fir compiled it as a branch to a fallback `dyn _base(<constants>)` and a merge phi of type `V`. The fallback was also wrong: it called the base function with unevaluated arguments. Its symbol constants counted as loads, so variables like sieve's `primes` stayed in the frame, and the `V` phi hid the result type; sieve, queens, bounce and bounce_nonames paid for this in their loops.
solution: `BC2FirCFGCompiler` keeps the two lookups and the compare `_guard`, then adds a checkpoint and the assumption `_guard ?= TRUE`, which deoptimizes to the `BASEGUARD` instruction. The fallback block, the branch and the merge phi are gone, and the guard's label block gets no phi. This also removes the wrong fallback. Also in this range: the interpreter no longer restores into the same baseline forever when an assumption fails in the deopt-restore CFG (`b1db6ab94`), and the unboxed math1 builtins in `runtime.c` warn "NaNs produced" like GNU-R (`8b5b65993`), which the promotion of `x` in `inline_math1` exposed.

files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime.c: Adds `Fir_math1_result`, so the unboxed math1 builtins warn "NaNs produced" when a number becomes NaN.
files.repo-map.md: Adds `BaseGuardTest` and notes the base-guard deopt tests in the interpreter test directory.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/bc2fir/B: A `BASEGUARD` becomes a checkpoint with `_guard ?= TRUE` instead of a branch to a fallback call and a merge phi.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: The deopt-restore check compares the cursor's CFG, not the version's, so a failed baseline assumption errors instead of looping.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/bc2fir/B: New test: bc2fir compiles a `BASEGUARD` into an assumption whose deopt stack holds the values below the guard.
files.server/src/test/java/org/prlprg/fir/inte: New test: a version deopts into a guarded baseline, and a rebound function fails there instead of looping.
